patient.title: Cisplatin + etoposide + chest radiotherapy
patient.purpose: Chemotherapy and chest radiotherapy work together to treat lung cancer. Your team will explain the aim, possible benefit and alternatives for you.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin damages the DNA that cancer cells need to divide. It can also affect healthy cells.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, reduced urine, hearing changes or tingling.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with an enzyme used to copy and repair DNA. This can stop cancer cells growing and can also lower healthy blood counts.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, a sore mouth or feeling faint during an infusion.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Infusion reaction or low blood pressure

agents.name: Chest radiotherapy
agents.explanation: Radiotherapy directs radiation at the planned chest area. Its appointments and dose are set by the radiation oncology team.
agents.watch: Report painful swallowing, poor intake, skin changes, new cough or breathlessness.
risks: Sore skin in the treated area
Cough or breathing changes during or after treatment

phases.label: Two initial cycles with radiotherapy
phases.detail: Cisplatin on Days 1 and 8; etoposide on Days 1–5. Radiation appointments run alongside chemotherapy as planned by radiation oncology.

phases.label: Review before any further cycles
phases.detail: If the cancer has not progressed and treatment remains appropriate, the consultant may prescribe two additional cycles with an agreed radiation plan. These are not automatic.

phases.label: Recovery and next treatment decision
phases.detail: Your team reviews recovery and response, then agrees the next plan. Further drug treatment or surgery is a separate decision.

timeline.label: Etoposide only
timeline.text: A separate infusion on each of Days 2,3,4 and 5, with prescribed safety checks.

timeline.label: Radiotherapy: separate appointment plan
timeline.text: This band shows overlap with the chemotherapy cycle, not daily radiation or a fixed number of fractions. Follow your radiation calendar.

timeline.label: Check symptoms throughout
timeline.text: Symptoms can arise on any day, including after the last treatment.

day_groups.title: Both chemotherapy medicines
day_groups.body: Treatment after blood-test and symptom review. Radiotherapy usually begins close to this first treatment.
day_groups.action: Confirm both treatment plans and take only the prescribed support medicines.

day_groups.title: Etoposide each day
day_groups.body: Return for etoposide on each of these four days. Radiotherapy appointments may also be planned.
day_groups.action: The team checks blood results and symptoms before dosing. Report swallowing or breathing changes.

day_groups.title: No planned chemotherapy
day_groups.body: Follow the separate radiotherapy calendar. Anti-sickness medicines may continue as prescribed.
day_groups.action: Call if unwell; do not wait for the next infusion.

day_groups.title: Cisplatin only
day_groups.body: Return for the second cisplatin dose after safety checks. Extra drip fluids are needed; etoposide is not given today.
day_groups.action: Confirm today’s anti-sickness plan with the team.

day_groups.title: No further chemotherapy this cycle
day_groups.body: Continue any planned radiotherapy appointments and safety checks. Tiredness and swallowing symptoms can build up.
day_groups.action: Report new symptoms and keep the urgent contact plan available, including after treatment ends.

support.title: Your anti-sickness plan
support.text: Cisplatin days need a different plan from etoposide-only days. The team combines prevention and rescue medicines into one clear schedule. Do not repeat or add courses yourself.

support.title: Eating, drinking and swallowing
support.text: Report painful swallowing, weight loss or difficulty drinking early. The team can arrange pain relief, dietitian support or other help.

support.title: Fluids and kidney protection
support.text: Follow your individual drinking advice and report much less urine. Cisplatin needs drip fluids before and after dosing; tell staff if you cannot drink or feel swollen or breathless.

support.title: Other medicines and prevention
support.text: Bring a full medicine list. Ask before starting medicines, supplements or vaccines. Fertility and contraception advice should be agreed before treatment.

questions.a: Chemotherapy is planned on Days 1–5 and8 of each cycle. Radiotherapy has a separate appointment calendar; do not use this cycle diagram as the radiation timetable.

questions.q: How many cycles will I have?
questions.a: Two cycles are planned. Two further cycles may be offered only after review and a new confirmed plan.

questions.q: Can side effects continue after treatment?
questions.a: Yes. Keep reporting new or worsening symptoms after the last infusion or radiation session. The team agrees your follow-up checks.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Chemotherapy and radiotherapy are used together for selected people with Stage III lung cancer.
evidence.interpretation: Published results help guide discussion but do not predict your outcome. The source study was small and did not compare this regimen with another treatment.

patient.indication_text: NCCP 00456a: Stage III non-small-cell lung cancer
patient.schedule_summary: Cisplatin on Days 1 and 8; etoposide on Days 1–5. Each cycle lasts 28 days. Two cycles first; two more may be offered after review. Radiotherapy usually starts within 24 hours of the first chemotherapy dose; follow your separate radiation appointment plan.
patient.administration_text: Cisplatin 50 mg/m² over 1 hour with pre/post hydration on Days 1 and 8; etoposide 50 mg/m² over1 hour on each of Days 1–5. Visits also include safety checks and preparation. The radiation team confirms its separate dose, fractions and calendar.
patient.monitoring_summary: Before starting: full blood count, kidney and liver tests; hearing tests and creatinine clearance if clinically indicated. During treatment: NCCP blood counts on Days 1 and 8; etoposide product information adds blood counts before each etoposide dose, including Days 2–5. Kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Extra tests and response scans follow the individual plan.

monitoring_schedule.title: My tests and checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Required safety tests are distinct from team-agreed scans and follow-up. Radiotherapy appointments and extra tests follow your personal plan.

patient.urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, sudden illness, new or worsening breathlessness, troublesome bleeding, inability to drink or swallow, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine or severe rash. Tell staff at once about pain, swelling, faintness or breathing trouble during an infusion.
patient.consent_support: Discuss the aim and alternatives, blood-count suppression and serious infection, kidney/hearing/nerve injury, nausea, hair loss, infusion reactions, fertility, and chest radiation effects including swallowing and breathing problems. Etoposide for NSCLC is outside its licensed indication; explain the rationale and follow local off-label consent policy.

sections.title: Frequent visits in week 1
sections.text: Plan for chemotherapy on Days 1–5 plus Day 8. Radiation may require other visits; combine calendars with the team.

sections.title: After the visits
sections.text: Keep support medicines and contact numbers at hand. Ask early for help with swallowing, food, fluids or transport.

anatomy: Report ringing in the ears, hearing change or new tingling.
Report mouth sores, painful swallowing or difficulty drinking.
New or worsening cough or breathlessness needs prompt advice, during or after treatment.

Fever, chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding need immediate advice.
Tell the team about sore skin in the treated area, a spreading rash or increasing fatigue.

chronology_notes.text: Tiredness and swallowing discomfort may develop during treatment. Breathing changes can also appear later; report them after treatment as well.

rationale.summary: Cisplatin causes DNA damage; etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II. Concurrent thoracic radiation adds local tumour treatment, with overlapping marrow, mucosal and pulmonary toxicity requiring coordinated review.
rationale.line: Combined-modality Stage III treatment; multidisciplinary selection required
factors: Stage III NSCLC, ECOG0–1 and suitability for the complete chemoradiation plan.
alternatives: Other multidisciplinary local/systemic strategies, radiotherapy alone where appropriate, clinical trials and symptom-focused care; tailor to fitness, stage, biomarkers and patient priorities.
limitations: Both sources have gaps at exact blood-count boundaries; dose decisions require review.
NCCP blood-count reductions differ from current etoposide product information; the discrepancy is explicit.
Radiation dose, fractions, treatment breaks and any later treatment are separate specialist decisions.
The source has two initial cycles and two optional additional cycles; four cycles are not guaranteed.
SWOG9019 was a small historical single-arm study, not a comparison with current multimodal options.

medicines.name: Aprepitant
medicines.dose: 125 mg orally on the platinum day;80 mg on the next2 days

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.dose: 16 mg orally

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 12 mg orally on the platinum day;8 mg daily on the next3 days
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and any other steroids.

medicines.name: Olanzapine
medicines.dose: 5 mg orally on the platinum day and next3 days
medicines.note: Sedation, metabolic risk and other medicines require review.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally three times daily as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS high-risk row has no end-day orPRN qualifier. Confirm duration; coadministration with olanzapine increases extrapyramidal risk.

additional_support: Multiday SACT: reconcile antiemetics for each day’s medicines and the two days after; one combined prescription is required. Do not add independent overlapping courses.

Coordinate radiation-related nausea, swallowing, nutrition, skin care and respiratory assessment with radiation oncology.

Review etoposide interactions, live vaccines, nephrotoxic/ototoxic medicines and any duplicate QT-prolonging antiemetics.

Day 1 etoposide in 1 L may be considered prehydration; Day 8 has no etoposide infusion, so prescribe its own prehydration. Routine furosemide to induce urine flow is not recommended without fluid overload.

patient.safety_note: Call oncology immediately for fever, sudden illness, new or worsening breathlessness, troublesome bleeding, inability to drink or swallow, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine or severe rash. Tell staff at once about pain, swelling, faintness or breathing trouble during an infusion.

rationale.summary: Carboplatin causes DNA damage; etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II. Concurrent thoracic radiation adds local tumour treatment, with overlapping marrow, mucosal and pulmonary toxicity requiring coordinated review.
rationale.setting: Stage III non-small-cell lung cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable
rationale.line: Combined-modality Stage III treatment; multidisciplinary selection required
factors: Stage III NSCLC, ECOG0–1 and suitability for the complete chemoradiation plan.
alternatives: Other multidisciplinary local/systemic strategies, radiotherapy alone where appropriate, clinical trials and symptom-focused care; tailor to fitness, stage, biomarkers and patient priorities.
limitations: Both sources have gaps at exact blood-count boundaries; dose decisions require review.
NCCP blood-count reductions differ from current etoposide product information; the discrepancy is explicit.
Radiation dose, fractions, treatment breaks and any later treatment are separate specialist decisions.
NCCP 00561 supports two cycles; do not import optional extra cycles from cisplatin 00456.
The cited Albain2009 trial used cisplatin, not carboplatin AUC3. Its survival results must not be presented as a measured benefit for this regimen.

support_summary: Carboplatin days need a different plan from etoposide-only days. The team combines prevention and rescue medicines into one clear schedule. Do not repeat or add courses yourself.
Report painful swallowing, weight loss or difficulty drinking early. The team can arrange pain relief, dietitian support or other help.
Follow your individual drinking advice and report much less urine. Kidney tests help the team calculate your carboplatin dose; do not adjust it yourself.
Bring a full medicine list. Ask before starting medicines, supplements or vaccines. Fertility and contraception advice should be agreed before treatment.
baseline: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile. Isotope GFR preferred, otherwise verified GFR/CrCl estimate.
before_each_cycle: NCCP FBC weekly before treatment. Current etoposide SmPC additionally requires a blood count before each etoposide dose, including Days 2–5.
Renal and liver profile before each cycle; extra tests as clinically indicated.
ongoing: Radiation oncology confirms planning and reviews respiratory, swallowing and skin toxicity. Imaging, tumour-marker testing and follow-up timing are individually prescribed; no universal interval is specified.
Monitor fever/infection, nutrition, swallowing, hearing, peripheral nerves and respiratory symptoms.
administration: Carboplatin AUC3 over 30 minutes on Days 1 and 8; etoposide 50 mg/m² over1 hour on each of Days 1–5. Visits also include safety checks and preparation. The radiation team confirms its separate dose, fractions and calendar.
access: Appropriate IV access, facilities for anaphylaxis and monitored slow etoposide infusion; coordination with the radiation oncology plan.

evidence.population: Stage IIIA(N2) NSCLC suitable for the trial combined-modality strategy.
evidence.comparison: Cisplatin/etoposide chemoradiation followed by surgery versus continued definitive radiotherapy; not a carboplatin-AUC3 comparison.
evidence.applicability: Supports the combined-modality context only. Cannot assign a direct carboplatin-AUC3 efficacy estimate from a cisplatin trial.
evidence.qualitative_result: No direct regimen-specific comparative efficacy estimate is supplied here; the NCCP reference trial used a different platinum.

support_plans.label: Day 1 · Carboplatin + etoposide

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.dose: 16 mg orally

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 8 mg orally on the platinum day and next2 days

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily as required

additional_support: Multiday SACT: reconcile antiemetics for each day’s medicines and the two days after; one combined prescription is required. Do not add independent overlapping courses.
CarboplatinAUC3 is moderate risk here; do not import the AUC≥4 high-risk course simply because the drug is carboplatin.
Coordinate radiation-related nausea, swallowing, nutrition, skin care and respiratory assessment with radiation oncology.
No automatic routine G-CSF, antibacterial, antiviral or PJP prophylaxis is specified in these NCCP regimens; consider individual risk and local policy.
Review etoposide interactions, live vaccines, nephrotoxic/ototoxic medicines and any duplicate QT-prolonging antiemetics.
